newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ING to give employees free share options.
newsitem.headline: ING to give employees free share options.

text.p: Banking and insurance group Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV (ING) said on Tuesday it would give free options on new ING shares to its employees.

"Given the excellent results in 1996 but also because of the intended listing in New York, the management board has decided to make a one-off free offer of these options in 1997," ING wrote in its in-house magazine.
The options will give employees the right to buy ING shares during a five year period at a fixed price, equal to ING's opening share price on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange on May 23.
The bulk of ING's 58,000 employees will receive 100 options and a limited group of executives in higher salary scales will get 500 or 1,000 options.
ING said it had also set aside an unspecified number of options which unit managers could use to reward individual employees for outstanding achievements.
An ING spokesman said a maximum of 12 million new shares could be issued as a result of the staff options being exercised. ING currently has about 718 million ordinary shares outstanding.
